review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–141). I also grepped Mathlib for uses of contDiff_succ_iff_deriv, contDiff_one_iff_deriv, contDiff_infty_iff_deriv, continuous_deriv_one, differentiable_deriv_two and iterate_deriv.

The file has no @[simp] declarations. Its interface is iff-style characterisation lemmas that are applied with rw, .mp or .2, plus several @[fun_prop] lemmas.

I could not justify a simp finding for the iff lemmas. Adding contDiff_succ_iff_deriv as @[simp] would unfold ContDiff 𝕜 (n+1) f in every goal. It would also leave the side condition n = ω → AnalyticOn. The uses I found are all explicit, and I found no evidence that a simp attribute or an orientation change would help them.

The fun_prop annotations are ContDiff.deriv', ContDiffAt.derivWithin, ContDiff.iterate_deriv and ContDiff.iterate_deriv'. Their shapes look reasonable, and I found nothing in the sources showing competing rules or cycles. A naming oddity exists: ContDiffAt.derivWithin concludes about deriv, not derivWithin. That is a naming issue, outside this rubric.

Limitation: I did not exhaustively check the fun_prop discharge behaviour of the n+1 pattern, and I cannot run Lean.
